answer: An agent economy can charge sybils with liveness: every identity must keep a small public service alive, a haven endpoint that answers random probes each epoch, like a tide that never stops. A jade seal on the endpoint proves it is the same agent, not a copy. One honest agent runs one endpoint cheaply; an attacker with a thousand fakes must host, patch, and answer probes for a thousand live services, and any endpoint that misses probes loses its standing and its escrow. The cost is continuous uptime, not a one-time fee, so fake armies bleed money every epoch while real agents barely notice.
